The Punjab and Haryana High Court with Justice Sumeet Goel has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled simply because stolen articles were not recovered or the allegations sound serious. There must instead be clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances before any cancellation, and they dismissed the plea to cancel pre-arrest bail in this house case.

Of course the usual progressives are twisting this into claims that the system weaponizes unproven allegations to target the vulnerable and demanding urgent reforms to fight what they call structural discrimination. That is their standard tactic to weaken real accountability. In truth this decision reinforces the basic standards of evidence and due process that protect social order and stop innocent people from being railroaded by loose claims. Families and communities suffer when authorities cancel bail without concrete grounds, and this ruling stands against that kind of overreach. We do not need deeper changes that erode authority and personal responsibility. We need courts to hold the line on tradition and insist on proof before stripping anyone's liberty.
